result:
The proposed answer of 12 rests on a false step, so I cannot accept it.

The solution claims that every quasivariety of Sugihara algebras is a variety. That is wrong. Quasivarieties are generated by classes of algebras closed under isomorphism, subalgebras and products, and they need not be closed under homomorphic images. A quasivariety need not contain all the subdirectly irreducible members that a variety with the same generators would contain, so the quasivariety lattice is strictly larger than the subvariety lattice. The counting argument therefore only covers varieties and ignores most of the quasivarieties.

The amalgamation analysis also looks unreliable. It dismisses AP for S₅ because "the only automorphism is the identity," but that does not by itself show amalgamation fails. It also does not explain why S₃ and S₄ behave differently from S₅ and S₆. I did not work out the correct count myself, but it should come from the actual classification of quasivarieties of Sugihara algebras, and that is unlikely to give 12.

VERDICT: REJECT
